result:
I changed the schedule PDF so a new page starts only when the next row doesn't fit in the space left on the current page. I only checked that the file parses (`ruby -c`). I did not generate a PDF or run any tests, so the page-count and layout results are unverified.

The cause was in `app/helpers/class_schedules_pdf_helper.rb`. The table was cut into slices of 15 rows, and each slice ended with a forced new page, so pages with shorter rows were left partly empty.

The new code prints the header once, then adds rows one at a time. Before each row it measures the row's height. If the row doesn't fit, it starts a new page and repeats the header there. Rows are never split across pages, and the content and order are unchanged. The footer text (the star note and the custom class-schedule text) is printed once, after the last row.

- **Row measurement:** the height check uses a plain 9pt `FreeSans` table with padding of 2. It does not include the negative padding that `class_schedule_print_table` sets on the first and last columns. The estimate could therefore be slightly off, and I didn't check it against real output.
- **Footer space:** the star note and the footer text are not included in the space check. If the last row ends very near the bottom of the page, they may be pushed onto an extra page.
